question: do Policy Predictor prediction MAGNITUDES influence any downstream behaviour, or only the selected policy class?
method: static audit of every consumer of the PP prediction array in the repository, plus a runtime determinism probe

consumers_of_the_prediction_array.uses: pred.argmax(axis=1) for target CENTERED (argmin for REGRET)
consumers_of_the_prediction_array.note: pure argmax; ties resolved by numpy argmax to the lowest index, which is deterministic and does not compare magnitudes against any threshold

consumers_of_the_prediction_array.uses: select_policy(P) -> index; plus a diagnostic raw_softmax_tie flag and a score_vector_hash column
consumers_of_the_prediction_array.note: the selected index drives everything; the tie flag and hash are written to the frame for reporting

consumers_of_the_prediction_array.uses: sel = select_policy(pred, target); sel_ari = ari_te[range, sel]
consumers_of_the_prediction_array.note: the index is used to look up an ARI; magnitudes are discarded

magnitude_derived_columns.definition: np.isclose(top1, top2, atol=0.0) on the sorted prediction row
consumers: stage2c/verify_stage2c3_gates.py:138 -- asserts that reported rate equals 1.0 as an integrity check
magnitude_derived_columns.reproduced_in_materialisation: yes, 0 mismatches on all 3,165 rows for both arms
magnitude_derived_columns.assessment: this is the only magnitude-derived quantity anywhere in the path. It is diagnostic, it feeds no policy choice, weighting, threshold, interpolation or candidate score, and it reproduced exactly.

external_consumers_outside_the_pp_packag.searched: repository-wide for policy_selections / selected_policy_id / select_policy / predict_proba
found: PP-internal analysis and gate scripts only

runtime_determinism_probe.cause: scikit-learn accumulates per-tree contributions across threads during forest prediction; floating-point addition is non-associative, so the low bits depend on thread scheduling

conclusion.decision: freeze PP inference at n_jobs=1 for all Stage-4 execution
conclusion.rationale: serial prediction is bit-stable (0/3165 variation) and yields an identical argmax, so freezing it removes the nondeterminism at no scientific cost
conclusion.one_ulp_issue_classification: non-scientific numerical nondeterminism (floating-point reduction order), not a model or behaviour difference

frozen_pp_inference_policy.note: the outer benchmark worker count remains 8; this setting is internal to the PP estimator only
